newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATE: IFC SAYS GREEK BOURSE GOOD FOR DIVERSIFICATION.
newsitem.headline: UPDATE: IFC SAYS GREEK BOURSE GOOD FOR DIVERSIFICATION.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) revised its IFC share index for Greece with the addition of six stocks in its annual rebalancing, it said on Wednesday.

"The number of stocks included in the IFC global index for Greece (IFCG-Greece) has now increased to 59 shares of which 54 are also included on the IFC investable index for Greece," said Constantinos Grigoriadis, head market analyst for central and eastern European emerging markets.
The five new shares are the following:

The weight of the IFCG Greece index at end-September was 6.52 percent of the IFCG Europe-Middle East-Africa index (EMEA) and 0.94 percent of the IFCG composite. The IFCI Greece was 7.05 and 1.59 percent of the EMEA and composite respectively, he said.

"Central and eastern European emerging stock markets are the super stars of the year. Russia, Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic remained on the top five in the beginning of November," Grigoriadis said.
The Athens stock exchange's year-to-date performance is the 19th best so far out of 26 emerging markets covered by the IFC investable index.

"Something that is really worth mentioning is that the Greek stock market has a very low correlation with other major developed or developing markets, figures that support the case for investing in Greek stocks for simple diversification reasons," the IFC analyst said.
"Needless to mention the attractiveness and fundamentals of the market," he added.
